title: Extension of scalars
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category with coequalizers such that $X\otimes-$ and
$-\otimes X$ preserve colimits for every $X$. Let $\varphi\colon\mathcal R\to\mathcal S$ be
a morphism of monoid objects with $\mathcal R$ commutative. Then $\mathcal S$ is an
$\mathcal S$-$\mathcal R$-bimodule: it acts on itself on the left by $\mu_{\mathcal S}$,
and $\mathcal R$ acts on the right by $\mu_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal S\otimes\varphi)$. Every
$\mathcal R$-module object $M$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]) is an
$\mathcal R$-$\mathcal R$-bimodule ([lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules]). Their tensor
product over $\mathcal R$,
$$
\mathcal S\otimes_{\mathcal R}M=\operatorname{coeq}\Bigl(\mathcal S\otimes\mathcal R\otimes M
\rightrightarrows\mathcal S\otimes M\Bigr)
$$
of $\bigl(\mu_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal S\otimes\varphi)\bigr)\otimes M$ and
$(\mathcal S\otimes\gamma_M)\alpha$, is a left $\mathcal S$-module object, with
$\mathcal S$ acting on the first factor. A morphism $f$ goes to the map induced by
$\mathcal S\otimes f$. This defines the *extension of scalars* functor
$\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi\colon\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)\to\Mod_{\mathcal S}(\mathcal C)$.

proof.text:
Write $R=\mathcal R$, $S=\mathcal S$, $\mu=\mu_S$, $\eta=\eta_S$, and $r=\mu\circ(S\otimes\varphi):S\otimes R\to S$. The following are identities of morphisms, with $\varrho$ denoting the right unitor. The monoid and monoid-morphism axioms of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] give
$$
r\circ(S\otimes\eta_R)=\varrho_S,\qquad
r\circ(S\otimes\mu_R)=r\circ(r\otimes R)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{S,R,R},\qquad
r\circ(\mu\otimes R)=\mu\circ(S\otimes r)\circ\alpha_{S,S,R}.
$$
The first equation uses $\varphi\eta_R=\eta$ and the right unit law of $\mu$; the second uses $\varphi\mu_R=\mu(\varphi\otimes\varphi)$ and associativity of $\mu$; the third is associativity of $\mu$ with its last input precomposed by $\varphi$. Together with the regular left $S$-action $\mu$, these are precisely the right-module unit and associativity axioms and the commuting-action axiom for the $S$-$R$-bimodule $S$. No commutativity of $S$ or centrality of the image of $\varphi$ is used.

source.place: First sentence: the bimodule axioms for S

proof.text: For a left $R$-module $M$ as in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], [lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules] equips it with the right action $\gamma_M\beta_{M,R}$ commuting with its left action. Its hypotheses hold because $\mathcal C$ is braided and $R$ is commutative. In constructing $S\otimes_R M$ only its original left action $\gamma_M$ is used.

source.place: Second sentence: M is a bimodule

proof.text: Put $D_M=(S\otimes R)\otimes M$, $B_M=S\otimes M$, $d_0=r\otimes M$ and $d_1=(S\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha_{S,R,M}$. Choose $q_M:B_M\to Q_M$ to be their coequalizer, which exists by hypothesis. This is the colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the small category with two objects and two parallel nonidentity arrows: a cocone with vertex $Z$ is exactly a map $h:B_M\to Z$ satisfying $h d_0=h d_1$, with its other leg necessarily $h d_0$. Thus $q_M d_0=q_M d_1$ and each such $h$ factors uniquely through $q_M$. In particular, if $u q_M=v q_M$ then $u=v$, since both are the unique factorization of that same cocone. This proves the cancellation property directly, rather than assuming a separate theorem about epimorphisms.

source.place: Stacks tag 002F (categories-definition-colimit), specialized to the parallel-pair category; compare tag 002A (categories-definition-coequalizers)

proof.text: For every object $X$, the assumption that $X\otimes-$ preserves colimits means, applied to the parallel-pair diagram of step 3, that $X\otimes q_M$ is again a coequalizer of $X\otimes d_0$ and $X\otimes d_1$. Its universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] gives the same cancellation property proved in step 3. Applying the hypothesis twice shows that $S\otimes q_M$ and $S\otimes(S\otimes q_M)$ both permit cancellation; associators identify the latter with $(S\otimes S)\otimes q_M$. No assertion that tensoring preserves arbitrary epimorphisms is needed.

source.place: Sentence beginning Since S tensor - preserves coequalizers

proof.text:
Define the multiplication maps
$$
t_B=(\mu\otimes M)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{S,S,M}:S\otimes B_M\to B_M,
$$
$$
t_D=((\mu\otimes R)\otimes M)\circ(\alpha^{-1}_{S,S,R}\otimes M)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{S,S\otimes R,M}:S\otimes D_M\to D_M.
$$
The third identity of step 1 gives $t_B(S\otimes d_0)=d_0t_D$. Tensor bifunctoriality, naturality of the associator and its pentagon axiom give $t_B(S\otimes d_1)=d_1t_D$: on either side the first two $S$ factors are multiplied by $\mu$, and the $R,M$ factors are acted on by $\gamma_M$. Thus $h_M=q_Mt_B$ satisfies
$$
h_M(S\otimes d_0)=q_Md_0t_D=q_Md_1t_D=h_M(S\otimes d_1).
$$
By the universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the preserved coequalizer from step 4, there is a unique map $a_M:S\otimes Q_M\to Q_M$ satisfying $a_M(S\otimes q_M)=q_Mt_B$. This is the required action on the first factor; the equality for $d_0$ uses exactly the associativity law of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] expanded in step 1.

source.place: Sentences saying mu_S tensor M is compatible with the parallel maps and descends to an action

proof.text:
For the unit axiom, precompose the two maps $\mathbf1\otimes Q_M\to Q_M$ with $\mathbf1\otimes q_M$. Tensor bifunctoriality, step 5, the left unit law of $\mu$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and naturality of the left unitor give respectively
$$
a_M(\eta\otimes Q_M)(\mathbf1\otimes q_M)
=a_M(S\otimes q_M)(\eta\otimes B_M)
=q_Mt_B(\eta\otimes B_M)
=q_M\lambda_{B_M}
=\lambda_{Q_M}(\mathbf1\otimes q_M).
$$
Here $t_B(\eta\otimes B_M)=\lambda_{B_M}$ is the left unit law of $\mu$ tensored with $M$, with the monoidal unitor axiom. Step 4 with $X=\mathbf1$ proves cancellation of $\mathbf1\otimes q_M$ directly from the coequalizer uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. It follows that $a_M(\eta\otimes Q_M)=\lambda_{Q_M}$, exactly the unit axiom of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects].

source.place: Sentence on the unit law after descending

proof.text:
For associativity, precompose the two maps $(S\otimes S)\otimes Q_M\to Q_M$ in the module axiom with $((S\otimes S)\otimes q_M)$, which permits cancellation by step 4 with $X=S\otimes S$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Tensor bifunctoriality, associator naturality and the equation defining $a_M$ reduce the composites of $a_M(\mu\otimes Q_M)$ and $a_M(S\otimes a_M)\alpha_{S,S,Q_M}$ respectively to
$$
q_Mt_B(\mu\otimes B_M)\quad\hbox{and}\quad q_Mt_B(S\otimes t_B)\alpha_{S,S,B_M}.
$$
After substituting $t_B=(\mu\otimes M)\alpha^{-1}_{S,S,M}$, the two expressions agree by the associativity equation for $\mu$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object] tensored with $M$ and the pentagon axiom for $\alpha$. Thus cancellation gives precisely the associativity axiom of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and $(Q_M,a_M)$ is a left $S$-module.

source.place: Sentence on the associativity law after descending

proof.text: Let $f:M\to N$ be $R$-linear in the sense of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Tensor bifunctoriality gives $(S\otimes f)d_0^M=d_0^N(S\otimes R\otimes f)$, and $f\gamma_M=\gamma_N(R\otimes f)$ gives $(S\otimes f)d_1^M=d_1^N(S\otimes R\otimes f)$. Hence $q_N(S\otimes f)$ coequalizes $d_0^M,d_1^M$. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] produces a unique map $\bar f:Q_M\to Q_N$ with $\bar f q_M=q_N(S\otimes f)$.

source.place: Sentence saying S tensor f is compatible with the parallel maps

proof.text:
To check that $\bar f$ is $S$-linear [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], write $t_B^M$ and $t_B^N$ for the maps $t_B$ of step 5 for $M$ and $N$. Precompose the desired equality with $S\otimes q_M$. Steps 5 and 8, tensor bifunctoriality and associator naturality give
$$
\bar f a_M(S\otimes q_M)=\bar f q_Mt_B^M=q_N(S\otimes f)t_B^M=q_Nt_B^N(S\otimes(S\otimes f)).
$$
The other side is explicitly
$$
a_N(S\otimes\bar f)(S\otimes q_M)=a_N(S\otimes(\bar f q_M))=a_N(S\otimes q_N)(S\otimes(S\otimes f))=q_Nt_B^N(S\otimes(S\otimes f)).
$$
Cancel $S\otimes q_M$ using its coequalizer universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], obtaining $\bar f a_M=a_N(S\otimes\bar f)$.

source.place: Sentence saying the descended map is S-linear

proof.text: The maps assigned to $\mathrm{id}_M$ and $\mathrm{id}_{Q_M}$ have the same composite $q_M$ with $q_M$, and for $M\xrightarrow{f}N\xrightarrow{g}P$ both $\overline{g f}$ and $\bar g\bar f$ have composite $q_P(S\otimes(g f))$ with $q_M$. Uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] therefore gives $\overline{\mathrm{id}_M}=\mathrm{id}_{Q_M}$ and $\overline{g f}=\bar g\bar f$. Composition in the module category is underlying composition [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], so the constructed object and morphism assignments define exactly the stated functor $\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$.
